changes: Beta 7 - free until October 15

This Beta needs no license and has no trial limit: every conversion is complete, until October 15, 2026 included. The License section and the trial are switched off in this Beta and come back with the official release
The title reads "CrossFlow BETA 7", and logs stay on, as in the previous Betas
Clip colors

Clip colors now follow your own Premiere Pro labels: CrossFlow reads the colors your labels really have and gives each one the closest DaVinci Resolve clip color, while keeping different labels on different colors as much as possible. Before, the right colors were only transferred if your Premiere Pro labels had been set up to look like Resolve's

New "Match Premiere Labels to Resolve" button in the Settings & License tab: it switches Premiere Pro's 16 labels to DaVinci Resolve's 16 clip colors, so a clip looks exactly the same in both applications. Premiere Pro must be open
DaVinci Resolve
On Windows, CrossFlow now works with DaVinci Resolve Studio installed in any folder or on any drive, not only in its default location
When DaVinci Resolve Studio is not installed on the computer, the conversion now says so clearly, instead of a generic conversion error
Bug reports

The Logs Zip now also contains DaVinci Resolve's preferences (Fairlight audio setup included) and Resolve's own log, and the conversion log notes Resolve's version, the page it was on and the new project's settings. Some conversion problems only happen with one particular Resolve setup: this is what lets us find which one
Settings

New "Do not check for updates or news at startup" setting in the Settings & License tab: CrossFlow then never contacts GitHub on its own, only when you click a link, for computers that must not reach the internet by themselves
The documentation now gives the correct minimum macOS version: macOS Monterey (12.0) or more recent. Big Sur (11.0) was listed by mistake
Audio tracks

Fixed a conversion that failed with "An error happened while Converting your project to Resolve" when DaVinci Resolve refused to create one of the sequence's audio tracks (seen with 8-channel Adaptive tracks). The track is now created as a Stereo track instead, so its clips are still converted, and the Full Details say which tracks were affected
If a track cannot be created at all, the conversion now carries on without it, and the Full Details list each clip that was left out and why
Full Details now show the errors of each timeline track. Before, a track that could not be created was never mentioned there
Sequence names

A sequence whose name contains "/" or "\" is now converted: DaVinci Resolve does not accept these characters in a timeline name, so they become "-" and Full Details says so. Before, such a sequence was not created, its clips were placed in another sequence's timeline, and the conversion could fail
If DaVinci Resolve cannot create a timeline, that sequence is now reported as an error and the rest of the project is still converted
Faster conversions
When Transcode is on but no clip of the project needs transcoding, CrossFlow no longer opens Premiere Pro: it goes straight to the conversion. Before, Premiere Pro was launched for nothing
Installing and uninstalling

The Mac download now includes "Uninstall CrossFlow": it removes the CrossFlow application and its Premiere Pro panel. An option, unticked by default, also deletes your CrossFlow settings, presets, logs and this computer's license activation

The old manual install/uninstall scripts for the Premiere Pro panel are gone from the download, and the Mac download no longer has a "CrossFlow Panel" folder at all: they were left over from earlier Betas, the installer sets up everything
Sequence selection

With "Convert Only Selected Sequences" on and no sequence ticked, Analyze Project and Convert now stop straight away and say so. Before, the conversion ran anyway and created a DaVinci Resolve project with no timeline. This is easy to hit after choosing another project, since that clears the sequence selection
CrossFlow licensing
CrossFlow now has a License section in the Settings & License tab: paste your license key and click "Activate License" to unlock the full conversion on this computer

One license activates CrossFlow on 2 computers. "Deactivate License" frees this computer again, so you can move your license to another one - up to twice a month, which covers a new machine or a reinstall
Lost, sold or broken computer? A link in the License section releases every computer on your license at once, so you can activate the one you actually have without waiting for support
The title reads CrossFlow PRO once your license is active, so you can always see at a glance whether this computer is licensed
CrossFlow only re-checks your license about once a week, and keeps working for a month with no internet at all - editing suites with no network stay perfectly usable

Without a license, CrossFlow now runs as a trial: only the first clips of each sequence are converted, counted separately for video and for audio. Everything else works normally, so you can check the conversion on your own real project before buying

Beyond that limit, video clips are replaced on the timeline by a CrossFlow placeholder image so the edit keeps its shape, and every clip concerned is listed in the conversion details with the reason - nothing disappears silently
A "Purchase" button opens the CrossFlow page so you can get a license
Anonymous usage statistics

To decide what to improve next, CrossFlow now sends anonymous statistics at the end of each conversion and once per week of use: the versions in use, the project's size and clip counts rounded into ranges, which options were used, whether the conversion succeeded and which kinds of problems it met. No project names, no file names and no media paths are ever sent, and nothing identifies you or your computer
A notice explains this the first time you open CrossFlow. You can turn it off at any time in the new "Usage Statistics" section of the Settings & License tab

A second, off-by-default option adds a random install ID, so that CrossFlow's usage over time and its trial limits can be understood. The ID is created on your computer, is not linked to your license or your email, and is deleted the moment you turn the option off
"See exactly what is sent" in that section shows the real content, waiting to be sent and already sent, so you never have to take our word for it
The Privacy Policy on nablast.com and the license agreement now describe everything CrossFlow sends over the network: license activation, the update check, and these statistics
New features:
Horizontal Flip and Vertical Flip effects are now transferred by the conversion from Premiere to Resolve
A keyframed clip now keeps its Blend Mode
Reliability improvements:
Fixed a conversion failing at the very last step on DaVinci Resolve versions older than 20.2, right after the timeline had been built, because of a clip renamed which was not supported at that time.
Keyframed Motion, Crop, Opacity, Volume and Pan are now transferred natively

Position, Scale, Rotation, Anchor Point, Crop, Opacity, Volume and Pan keyframes are now converted into real DaVinci Resolve keyframes you can still select and adjust, instead of being baked into a transcoded file. Premiere's easing is reproduced as well, including custom Bezier handles and both Spatial and Temporal Interpolation, so curved motion paths stay curved and eased moves keep their acceleration

As a result, a clip whose only special property is animated Motion, Crop, Opacity, Volume or Pan is no longer transcoded at all - conversions are faster and the media stays untouched. Clips with animated per-channel Volume or Blend Mode have no Resolve equivalent and are still transcoded as before
Crop (Left, Right, Top and Bottom) is now transferred as well, static or keyframed, and converts exactly with one Resolve keyframe per Premiere keyframe

Volume fades keep their exact shape: Premiere works in raw audio level and Resolve in decibels, so CrossFlow reproduces the curve to within a quarter of a decibel - about four times finer than anything you can hear

New Transcode option "Force Transcode of Keyframed Clips" (off by default, under "Optional baking"): turn it on if you would rather have the animation burned into the media so it matches Premiere exactly, at the cost of no longer being adjustable in Resolve
New Transfer option "Transfer Keyframes" (on by default): turn it off to skip the keyframe transfer entirely and fall back to static values, to help narrow down a problem in a converted project
Time Remapping is now transferred natively

A clip's Time Remapping is now converted into a real DaVinci Resolve retime curve you can still open and edit in the Retime Curve editor, instead of being baked into a transcoded file. Every speed keyframe lands on the matching frame, and the clip keeps its timeline length
Any handle rotation on Time Remapping is re-sampled until every rendered frame in Resolve shows the exact same frame of your footage as Premiere

Premiere and DaVinci Resolve disagree about which source frame to show when a speed ramp lands a hair away from a frame boundary - Premiere takes the earlier frame, Resolve rounds up into the next. CrossFlow now compensates, so both applications show the same frame of your footage on every frame of a retimed clip

A clip can carry a Speed change or Reverse Speed on top of its Time Remapping. Premiere keeps those two separate while Resolve has a single retime per clip, so CrossFlow now folds them together - a reversed retimed clip plays backwards through its own speed keyframes instead of losing one of the two

As a result, a Time Remapped clip is no longer transcoded by default. "Force Transcode of Time Remapped Clips" is now off by default and has moved to "Optional baking" - turn it on if you would rather have the speed changes burned into the media
See exactly what happened to your keyframes

Full Details now reports, for every animated clip, which controls were transferred natively as real Resolve keyframes - and, when CrossFlow had to add keyframes to follow a curve Resolve cannot express directly, how many each one gained
Project Content gained a "Keyframed Clips" total
Analyze Project gained an "Estimated Keyframe Transfer" section, listing ahead of time which clips will have their animation transferred and which controls are expected to gain extra keyframes
Unused clips are no longer imported into the Media Pool

New Transfer option "Skip Unused Project Items" (on by default, under "Media Pool"): the converted DaVinci Resolve project now only receives the clips its timelines actually use, instead of a copy of the whole Premiere Project Panel

This covers the three ways a clip ends up unused: never placed in a timeline, only used by sequences left out by the sequence filter, or an original clip whose every occurrence was replaced by its transcoded version
Full Details reports how many clips were left out. Turn the option off to import everything as-is, unused clips included
Your Premiere Proxies are now attached in DaVinci Resolve too

New Transfer option "Attach Premiere Proxies" (on by default, under "Media Pool"): a clip that has a Proxy attached in Premiere now gets the very same proxy file attached in Resolve, through Resolve's own proxy mechanism, so you can switch between full resolution and proxy in Resolve exactly as you did in Premiere
The existing proxy file is only linked, never copied nor re-encoded, so it costs no extra disk space and no extra conversion time
Full Details reports how many proxies were attached, and names any proxy whose file is no longer on disk
Resolve is less permissive than Premiere for proxies (framerate needs to match for example), in that case feedback will report every proxies which could not be attached
Decide what happens to your Lumetri Color grade

A colour grade has three sensible outcomes, so Lumetri Color now has its own control in the Transcode Options: transcode the clip to keep the grade, keep the grade if the clip is transcoded anyway (the default), or always discard it

"Always discard the grade" renders those clips ungraded, ready to grade from scratch in DaVinci Resolve. Your own project is never touched: CrossFlow already renders from a throwaway copy, and switches the grade off only inside that copy
Choose which effects are worth a transcode
Two general main Video/Audio effects checkboxes come with the list of effects your project actually uses, one checkbox each, under "Effects Found In This Project"

Untick the effects you do not mind losing, or that DaVinci Resolve handles well enough on its own, and the clips carrying only those keep their original media. A clip carrying an unticked effect alongside a ticked one is still transcoded, which bakes in both
Each effect shows how many clips use it, so the ones worth a decision come first, and there is a search box for projects with a long list
Warp Stabilizer is applied as Resolve's own Stabilization, so is unticked by defautlt, but stays adjustable there. Tick it to bake Premiere's exact result in

Your choices are remembered from project to project, so an effect you never want to trigger a transcode only needs unticking once. Effects unticked on other projects are listed under the two lists, with a Reset All button
Whatever you untick, Full Details still reports those clips as reduced fidelity, so nothing is lost silently
Linked Video/Audio clips stay linked

A clip and the audio that came with it were linked in Premiere but arrived unlinked in DaVinci Resolve, so moving or trimming one left the other behind. They now stay linked, whatever the link looks like: a clip with several audio items such as a multi-channel camera file, an audio half slipped out of sync, a video half trimmed shorter than its audio, or a Merged Clip whose picture and sound come from different files
New Transfer option "Transfer Linked Clips" (on by default): turn it off to get the previous behaviour and have every clip land on its own
Improvements:
New button to select the current project running and ative in Premiere Pro
Disabled effects in Premiere are now ignored by CrossFlow, not making a Transcode action because of that anymore for example
CrossFlow now saves your project in Premiere before reading it, so anything you had edited in Premiere without saving is now properly converted to Resolve
Your original Premiere project is never written to, and CrossFlow only works on a copy to not modify it
Project analysis is about twice as fast
Clearer analysis and transcode reporting
Click any option name to read about it, opening automatically the documentation tab at the section explaining it
Reliability improvements:

Selecting a new project now unselects every sequence. The sequences you had ticked were being carried over by position, so a different project could silently end up converting sequences you never picked
Fixed some error messages being shown with an information icon instead of an error one, which made a real failure look like a harmless notice
Fixed the New Project Name you typed being discarded the next time CrossFlow started, instead of being remembered like every other option

Fixed the "Converted" total in Full Details counting more items than were actually converted: clips left out by "Skip Unused Project Items" were counted as converted, and every attached proxy counted its clip a second time. Both are still reported on their own line, they just no longer inflate the total

CrossFlow no longer shows error messages inside Premiere Pro. The invisible panel CrossFlow runs there reports any problem straight back to the CrossFlow application, which is where you are actually looking, instead of leaving a notification behind in Premiere Pro that nothing was waiting on

Fixed a reversed clip showing the wrong frame of your footage whenever its Speed was not 100%. A clip at -200% was a whole frame out, and this affected every reversed speed change, with or without Time Remapping. Reversed clips at 100% were already correct and are unchanged

Fixed the Motion Anchor Point placing the image in the wrong spot in DaVinci Resolve at any scale other than 50%. Premiere and Resolve handle the Anchor Point differently - in Premiere it moves the image, in Resolve it only sets the pivot - so CrossFlow now compensates on Position as well, and the image lands exactly where Premiere had it at every scale

CrossFlow no longer hangs indefinitely in the Transcoding step if Adobe Media Encoder crashes or is closed mid-transcode - the affected clips are now marked as failed and the process continues instead

Fixed clips coming from an After Effects composition (Dynamic Link) always failing to transcode, with Adobe Media Encoder reporting "Encoding error (9007)". Premiere names such a clip "Composition/File.aep", and that slash was being carried into the name of the file to write, sending Media Encoder at a folder that does not exist. Any character Windows forbids in a filename is now replaced by an underscore
Fixed two clips sharing the same source media overwriting each other in Return to Premiere - the number added to keep their exported filenames apart was being swallowed

Interpret Footage frame rates now reach DaVinci Resolve, including the ones Resolve only offers as "Custom" in Clip Attributes - 20, 15 or 35 fps, say. They were being silently replaced by 24 fps, which then made the clip look shorter than it is and failed its conversion with a message about the clip being longer than its media. A frame rate CrossFlow still cannot apply is now reported on the clip itself instead
Fixed the H264 MP4 Adaptive Bitrate and Fixed Bitrate Encoding Presets failing to transcode on macOS, with an error about preparing the bitrate preset
Reliability improvements

Fixed an issue in Windows where converting could crash, or DaVinci Resolve itself could become unresponsive on launch, unless a Python installation exactly matching the one CrossFlow relies on already happened to be present on the system. CrossFlow now installs its own compatible Python automatically in Windows, so nothing needs to be installed separately
Fixed CrossFlow's background Premiere Pro panel becoming unresponsive when it detected a mismatched engine version on startup
Faster Transcoding via Adobe Media Encoder
Clips are now queued to Adobe Media Encoder in a single batch instead of one at a time, significantly speeding up Automatic Transcoding
Reliability improvements
Fixed a rare cache-file conflict that could happen when a project's Sequence List and Project Info were both requested at the same time
Return to Premiere's Replace step no longer unnecessarily re-saves your original Premiere Pro project

If DaVinci Resolve's scripting engine crashes unexpectedly while converting a project, CrossFlow now shows a clearer message explaining it and suggesting to fully close DaVinci Resolve before retrying, instead of a generic error
New: Automatic Transcoding via Adobe Media Encoder

Clips or effects DaVinci Resolve can't reproduce natively - unsupported Video/Audio Effects, Time Remapping, Masks/Mask AI, Adjustment Layers with an effect, After Effects Dynamic Link (.aep) and After Effects Graphics (.aegraphic) clips, Titles/Graphics with alpha - are now automatically rendered through Adobe Media Encoder before conversion, so the visual/audio result is preserved instead of lost
Fully configurable: enable/disable Transcoding entirely, or toggle each clip category independently
Choose the output folder and the filename suffix used for transcoded media
Transitions (e.g. a Cross Dissolve) between a transcoded clip and its neighbor are preserved by baking the transition directly into the transcoded clip
Cineform RGB 12-bit / GoPro Cineform RGB 16-bit is only offered as an Encoding Preset on Windows, since it's not available on macOS
New: Return to Premiere

Once clips have been color graded in DaVinci Resolve (a Color Node applied), CrossFlow can now detect them, export them out of Resolve, and automatically build a new Premiere Pro project with the graded clips already placed back in
Started directly from a past conversion in the new Results tab, with a confirmation step before running
Choose the exported clips' filename suffix and the new project's save location
New: Results tab with full Task History
Every conversion, and every Return to Premiere run, is now saved and reviewable later, including after closing and reopening CrossFlow
See the full source project analysis, the options used, and a detailed per-clip breakdown of what was converted, transcoded, or flagged (warnings/errors), with rendered file reasons and sizes
Live progress is shown in the Results tab while a task is running
Delete past results you no longer need
New: Notifications and progress tracking
Native OS notification when a process finishes (can be disabled in Settings & License)
Taskbar (Windows) / Dock (macOS) icon now shows a live progress bar for the running process
CrossFlow automatically comes back to the front if Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve steal window focus while a process is running, without interrupting a dialog you need to interact with in either app
New Transferable item: Warp Stabilizer
Clips with the Warp Stabilizer effect applied are now transferred, with DaVinci Resolve's own Stabilization applied to match
New Transferable item: Track Mute and Solo
Timeline tracks that are Muted (Video and Audio) or Soloed (Audio) in Premiere Pro now keep that same state on the converted DaVinci Resolve timeline
Now officially supporting DaVinci Resolve 21.0.3
Reliability improvements
Premiere Pro is launched independently from CrossFlow, so closing CrossFlow doesn	 close Premiere Pro mid-process
Various fixes around transcoding and replacing clips back into the project (audio track mute/unmute handling, filename/import edge cases, AI Mask detection)
Fixed a replaced Title/Graphic sometimes leaving a leftover, overlapping clip behind on the timeline instead of being fully replaced
Clips with animated (keyframed) Position, Scale, Rotation, Anchor Point, Opacity, Volume, or Pan are now properly preserved via Automatic Transcoding instead of silently losing the animation
Interface improvements
Redesigned results/feedback screens with clearer icons and before/after project indications
Options and buttons are hidden while a process is running, to keep the interface focused on progress
New background interactive look, can be disabled from the Settings tab
A lot more to come: keep sending your feedback at contact@nablast.com, it directly shapes what gets built next!
First Release of CrossFlow
Windows 11 and Mac from 12.0 supported
Adobe Premiere Pro projects created from 13.0 (Premiere Pro CC 2019)
DaVinci Resolve Studio from 20.0 (not tested in Beta 21.X yet)

Supported while converting your Premiere Pro Project to DaVinci Resolve:
Multiple Timelines with different Framerates or Resolutions
Different Timeline Audio Tracks Config (Mono, Stereo, 5.1, ..)
Nested Sequences
Multicam Sequences
Timeline Clip classical effects, such as Opacity, BlendMode, Position, Scale, Anchor, Audio Volume, Pan, ..
Timeline Clip Speed Changed and/or Reversed
Timeline Clip Name and Colors
Some Audio and Video Transitions
Framerate Interpreted Footages
Image Sequences and Hold Frames
Project Bin Folder Structures
Project Item and Timeline Markers
